items.title: Tekken Chief Blasts Xbox Series S as a 'Weaker Child' Holding Back Developers
items.summary: Tekken producer Katsuhiro Harada told a developer conference in Korea that he wished hardware like the Xbox Series S had never been released, calling…
items.content:
Add preferred source Tekken producer Katsuhiro Harada told a developer conference in Korea that he wished hardware like the Xbox Series S had never been released, calling it a weaker sibling with awkwardly low performance. He argued the console's closeness to the Series X raises player expectations while forcing extra optimization work, and that complaints land on developers rather than Microsoft. Cyberpunk 2077 associate director Paweł Sasko said the hardware poses constant optimization challenges but also widened the audience and improved cross-platform code. Microsoft requires games to ship on both Xbox models with feature parity. Key Elements Katsuhiro Harada Tekken Xbox Series S Microsoft Paweł Sasko Cyberpunk 2077 CD Projekt Baldur's Gate 3 Wardogs Xbox Series X Nintendo Switch 2 Katsuhiro Harada, the longtime producer behind Bandai Namco's Tekken fighting game franchise, used a developer panel in Korea to deliver an unusually blunt critique of Microsoft's entry-level Xbox Series S, calling it a "weaker child" whose compromises ripple across the entire development pipeline.

Speaking during a roundtable at the Console Game Developers Conference, Harada noted that a senior Xbox executive was in the room before saying he wished "hardware like the Xbox Series S wouldn't be released," according to IGN. The remark drew laughter, but the veteran developer did not stop there. He turned to Paweł Sasko, associate game director on Cyberpunk 2077, and asked whether the Polish studio had quietly resented the console's constraints.

Sasko's reply was diplomatic. He said the machine "constantly throws challenges at us and forces us to optimize our code very cleanly" — a response Harada immediately recast as a polite way of saying the hardware falls short. The exchange underscored a tension that has run through the current console generation since the Series S arrived in 2020 as a cheaper, disc-less alternative to the Series X.

Harada's core complaint is not raw memory, though he acknowledged that is a factor. The harder problem, he argued, is that the Series S sits close enough to the Series X that players expect near-identical results, yet performs noticeably worse. Porting to a platform like Nintendo's successor console, by contrast, comes with a built-in reset in expectations, because developers can treat it as a distinct device aimed at a different audience. With Xbox, he said, teams deliver their best work and then face what feels like extra labor on behalf of a slightly weaker sibling.

He also pointed to the commercial math. In a market like the United States, Series S owners outnumber Series X owners, so studios cannot simply scale back support. When visual differences appear, he said, the complaints land on developers rather than on Microsoft, with players asking why texture resolution is lower only on the budget machine.

Microsoft's parity policy sits at the center of the dispute. The company requires that games ship on both Series X and Series S or on neither, and that the two versions retain feature parity. That rule has repeatedly forced studios into difficult engineering choices. Larian Studios brought Baldur's Gate 3 to Xbox months after other platforms and needed help from Microsoft engineers to get split-screen co-op running on the cheaper console. More recently, the team behind the breakout shooter Wardogs said Series S limitations kept certain features out of the game.

Sasko, for his part, offered a counterweight. He conceded the drawbacks are real but said the console's lower price has widened the audience for games, and that optimization work first done for the Series S ended up improving Cyberpunk 2077 on every platform. Harada closed by joking that the discussion might leave Microsoft feeling reassured enough to launch a lower-powered successor to its next-generation console.

That next-generation machine, referred to in reports as Helix, has been the subject of shifting launch estimates, with some pointing to a holiday 2027 debut and later ones suggesting 2028 at a price range of $1,200 to $1,800.

Harada's standing gives the comments weight. As the face of Tekken for years, he has built a reputation for speaking his mind, and few figures of comparable seniority have criticized the Series S so openly. His remarks land as Microsoft tries to court developers for its next hardware cycle while defending a two-tier strategy that has shaped this generation's Xbox software.

For publishers, the practical takeaway is familiar: the Series S remains a mandatory target, and its constraints translate into schedule risk and engineering cost that must be absorbed somewhere. For Microsoft, the risk is less about one producer's quip than about whether the parity requirement becomes a deterrent when studios weigh where to allocate resources. For players, the debate is a reminder that the cheapest way into a console ecosystem often comes with trade-offs that surface later, in the form of delayed releases and trimmed features.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Is Now Available On Battle.net
Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 Is Out Now With Cross-Platform Mods and Dual Wielding
items.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 Is Out Now With Cross-Platform Mods and Dual Wielding From Fextralife (Written by Laura-May Randell) on November 11, 2026 | OpenCritic

Cyberpunk 2077 has received its free Edgerunners 2 Update, and it introduces new gameplay features, anime-inspired content, and cross-platform mod support to CD Projekt Red's open-world RPG. Update 2.5 launched October 22 on Mac, PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S, with the Nintendo Switch 2 version expected in the coming days.

One of the most exciting additions in this update is the cross-platform mod support, which allows players to browse and install supported community-created content directly through the game's menu. So if you were tired of messing around with the game files, rejoice! Powered by mod.io , the feature is also planned for the Nintendo Switch 2, which will expand access to player-made content beyond PC and allow for mods on a near-unmoddable console.

The 2.5 update also introduces dual wielding for pistols and revolvers through the new Double Trouble perk in the Cool skill tree, because sometimes one is just not enough. Players can experiment with a different combat style while additional perks support this new approach to gunfights.

Fans of the Netflix anime have some new content to explore, too. There is a new Clampdown side quest, a five-piece gear...

items.title: Microstutters were wrecking my games, and one open-source tool finally told me why
items.summary: Stuttometer makes troubleshooting microstutters exponentially easier, even on Unreal Engine games.
items.content:
Gameplay from Phantom Blade Zero on PC. Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO Add MakeUseOf on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Suman Biswas Published Nov 9, 2026, 8:00 AM EST Suman is a Computer Science graduate with a passion for gaming and technology. His love for technology started when he first got his hands on an NES. An avid gamer and PC enthusiast at heart, Suman started his writing journey back in 2023. While gaming takes up most of his free time, Suman also dabbles in tinkering with PC builds and consoles. Sign in to your MakeUseOf account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap As much as I enjoy playing my games on PC, one issue makes me consider jumping back to consoles: microstutters.

You would think that with all the advancements in modern game engines, development pipelines, and consumer hardware, microstutters, or any form of hitching, would be a thing of the past. But unfortunately, that's not reality.

That's why when I came across a free diagnostic tool called Stuttometer, I knew my microstuttering problems were finally going to be fixed — and all it took was a few minutes of analysis.

SteamOS is ol' reliable when I want a Linux-gaming experience at this point.

Credit: Suman Biswas\/MUO "'; The idea of trying Stuttometer came from my somewhat rough experience with the recently released UE5 game Phantom Blade Zero . Unlike most Unreal Engine 5 releases this year, such as Silent Hill Townfall or Halo: Campaign Evolved , Phantom Blade Zero has no shader-related stutters. However, the latter, more open regions of the game are plagued by traversal stutters and microstutters, which severely hampered my experience.

What's even more annoying is that, despite my hours of testing and trying different settings, I couldn't figure out the root cause of the microstutters. With every passing year, we seem to be getting more and more games plagued by stuttering issues. What's even more egregious is how difficult it is to diagnose and troubleshoot microstutters, especially in Unreal Engine 5 games.

That is when I decided to give Stuttometer a shot. Now, unlike most gaming-related applications on GitHub, Stuttometer isn't a mod. It's essentially an overlay, akin to MSI Afterburner or RTSS. As such, you don't have to worry about having to meddle with your game's installation directory or save files.

Next, launch your game, and Stuttometer will automatically start recording data from the gameplay session. Additionally, you can press Ctrl+F11 to manually toggle background trace capture if you don't want to close the game. Once you finish recording a gameplay session, you can export the created JSON file with detailed stutter count and history.

Gameplay from Phantom Blade Zero on PC. Credit: Suman Biswas/MUO Generally, microstutters are a result of the game engine failing to render environment/scene assets on time. Previously, developers relied on triple-buffered V-sync to help eliminate microstutters. However, V-sync comes with its own downsides, such as incompatibility with FreeSync or G-sync-compatible displays. Furthermore, V-sync also comes with a substantial performance cost, without eliminating stutters.

Surprisingly enough, texture pop-in isn't the only culprit behind microstutters in modern PC games.

For instance, while testing Cyberpunk 2077 using Stuttometer, I found the game was relatively stutter-free even with all the ray-tracing bells and whistles enabled. However, whenever the game tries to auto-save, it causes a microstutter, which is the only stuttering Stuttometer registered.

Stutters can be the result of poor texture streaming, low memory bandwidth, and incomplete shader compilation

This essentially means that the microstutters in Cyberpunk 2077 have nothing to do with GPU or CPU utilization. Instead, most microstutters result from how the engine writes data to the SSD.

Similarly, in Phantom Blade Zero , most stutters come from the game's use of software RT for lighting. On Stuttometer, I saw a substantial difference in the frame-time graph by simply testing the game with RT enabled and disabled. Stuttometer also recommended recompiling shaders for the game and increasing the shader cache limit .

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 player drops free gameplay expansion that makes Night City feel alive
items.summary: Recent updates have already tackled initial issues, as well.
items.content:
A free Cyberpunk 2077 mod adds six NPC interactions, letting players recruit allies, challenge strangers, and confront police.

Cyberpunk 2077 has received a substantial free gameplay expansion from a player that introduces new ways to interact with Night City's inhabitants, including recruiting NPCs as allies, challenging strangers to fights, and even provoking confrontations with police.

The fan-made addition arrives as CD Projekt RED's sci-fi RPG continues to benefit from its dedicated modding community, which has spent years introducing features that expand the game's open-world activities and improve how its inhabitants behave.

Our favourites amongst previous creations so far have let players possess enemies , allowed players to explore Night City in third-person , and even a boost to the level cap — included in the 13 best mods of Cyberpunk 2077 we’d found so far. However, this latest release focuses specifically on making everyday encounters feel more meaningful, giving V several new ways to approach the city's population.

Created by modder Adriansito and released on Nexus Mods on October 26, Immersive NPCs introduces six additional interactions with others in Cyberpunk 2077 : Talk, Flirt, Provoke, Calm, Challenge and Goodbye.

Rather than requiring separate dialogue screens or custom menus, the expansion incorporates these features directly into Cyberpunk’s existing interaction system, with support for keyboard and controller inputs included.

The Talk feature, for instance, allows V to greet pedestrians, who respond with spoken dialogue without interrupting their movements or changing their attitude towards the player.

More notably, the Flirt interaction can convince NPCs to become followers through a two-step process; this allows V to recruit former enemies who will fight alongside them. However, police officers cannot be recruited this way.

Alternatively, Provoke allows players to deliberately antagonise characters, with different consequences depending on their targets. Ordinary civilians might surrender or flee, whereas enemies and police officers can respond by initiating combat.

Meanwhile, the Calm option can subsequently defuse a confrontation, while Challenge introduces non-lethal boxing matches against NPCs, including recruited companions, with opportunities to earn additional eddies.

Finally, Goodbye allows V to dismiss followers and restore their original faction allegiances.

As the mod's description explains: “Talk to the city. Flirt with the right people. Provoke the wrong ones.”

Since the Cyberpunk 2077 mod’s initial release, the expansion has received several updates introducing additional dialogue options, improvements to recruited allies, and fixes targeting conflicts with stealth takedowns.

Some players have reported crashes and controller input issues, but the mod’s uploader — ‘Suprt132’ — has been quick to notify users of new incoming updates that address major problems being had.

items.title: 5 Cheaper Ways To Play Games Than Building A New PC In 2026
items.summary: If inflated RAM and SSD prices have made building a new gaming PC a far-fetched dream, handhelds and cloud gaming can be great alternatives for budget gaming.
items.content:
DC Studio/Shutterstock Add BGR on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Assembling your own rig, choosing every fine detail, including the CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, motherboard, cooling system, power supply, and case, is satisfying, despite being an involved process. You'd think since you get to source the parts yourself, you'd come out with massive savings, but that has become hard due to the cost of RAM and NAND flash (the internal memory found in SSDs, flash drives, and memory cards) skyrocketing because of the supply shortage caused by the high demand in AI.

If you just want to play games without worrying about tinkering with a lot of settings and optimizations, a solid mid-range PC can handle those gaming needs. But according to the guide published by GamersNexus , a mid-ranger that will give you "smooth frame rates at 1440p in almost any game" will set you back about $1,500.

However, there are cheaper options that can get you gaming right away. Consider gaming handhelds, for example, that can run modern AAA titles in a portable form factor while costing a fraction of what gaming PCs do. And while we know console prices have risen sharply in recent times, they are still one of the most affordable ways to properly game. So, if you are a budget gamer like us, here are some other ways to game without breaking the bank.

FotoAndalucia/Shutterstock There are several handheld gaming PCs that can offer a decent experience, even though they can't max out the settings of modern AAA games. One of the most popular ones is the Steam Deck . It gives you access to a large library of AAA and indie PC games from Valve's massive platform, starting at $789.00 for the Steam Deck 512GB OLED. The Steam Deck gives comparable performance to the base PS4 , meaning you're looking at around 30 FPS for most modern AAA titles, but at a lower resolution of 800p versus the PS4's 1080p. Some games like "Pragmata" and "Control" can run at 60 FPS, but you need to make some performance optimizations (a huge advantage over consoles). There are also games that are Deck Verified, like "Cyberpunk 2077," "Elden Ring," and "The Witcher 3," which Valve guarantees work out of the box.

You can go cheaper with the ROG Xbox Ally at $599, but it's considered one of the weakest PC gaming handhelds. You can still play the latest games like "Gears of War: E-Day" via Game Pass if you tweak the resolution, frame rate, upscaling, and various other settings to reach the targeted 30 FPS. There are other gaming handhelds more powerful than the Steam Deck and the ROG Xbox Ally. However, they cost more, with the MSI Claw A8 BZ2EM costing $1299.99 at Best Buy.

Nattawit Khomsanit/Shutterstock Consoles are cheaper on average than PCs that can run current games optimally. For instance, while the PS5 Pro costs $899, building an equivalent rig can cost around $1,500 . But if the games you want to play on PC are also available on console, then getting a PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, or a Nintendo Switch 2 is the cheaper option. You just won't get access to the same settings and customization options as a PC, be able to freely download mods, or raid the deep discounts on multiple stores like Steam, Epic Games Store, and GOG.

Convenience is another thing consoles have over PCs. You just download a game or insert the disc, and you're guaranteed it will run. You don't have to worry about minimum or recommended specs. PCs have various configurations, which makes it harder for developers to come up with consistent specs needed to run games on every system.

Then you have first-party games. For example, legally, the major entries in "The Legend of Zelda," "Mario," and the "Pokémon" franchise can only be played on Nintendo systems. PlayStation tried its hand at releasing games on Steam, but has done a 180 on that strategy once things didn't work out. Games like "Wolverine," "Saros," and the upcoming "God of War Laufey" can only be played on the PlayStation 5. Xbox doesn't really do console-only exclusives since most of its first-party lineup is also available on PC from day one.

Redmagic Emulation allows you to play games meant for one system on another by simulating its hardware. Android devices are mostly used to simulate retro games, but PC emulation is something powerful gaming tablets can also do. A good example is the Redmagic Astra 2 , which packs a lot of performance features that make it ripe for PC emulation. It starts at $699 for the version with 12GB of RAM and 256GB of internal storage. The tablet runs on the flagship Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset and has a 9.06-inch OLED display with a 2,400x1,504 resolution and a refresh rate of 185Hz. It also has advanced liquid cooling for sustained gaming performance.

To play PC games on a tablet, you just need to install a PC emulator like GameHub . It allows you to connect your Steam account so you can download your purchased games and play them. However, since these gaming tablets still use mobile chipsets that prioritize efficiency over raw power, you'll have to lower the settings to achieve a playable experience.

Some games might also not work due to the game's launcher conflicting with the emulator. But with lowered graphics and GameHub's frame generation on, you can get 30-60 FPS performance on games like "The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt," "God of War: Ragnarok," and "Cyberpunk 2077." Also, tablets like the Redmagic Astra 2 have a dedicated Console Mode that allows you to send 4K video output to a TV and monitor via a USB cable.

Jess Rodriguez/Shutterstock With cloud gaming, your computer isn't running the game but receiving a video stream from a remote server where the game resides. The server is doing all the heavy lifting while you're just sending it the input via a controller or keyboard. You just need to find a subscription service with the games you want.

The most popular cloud gaming platform is Nvidia GeForce Now, with thousands of titles ready to play while enjoying GeForce RTX performance. It offers various plans, starting with the free ad-supported plan that has over 2,000 games, one-hour gaming sessions, and a resolution of up to 1080p at 60FPS. Paid plans start at $9.99 per month and increase the games, session hours, resolution, and frame rates. There's also Xbox Cloud Gaming, which comes with the Game Pass subscription, starting at $9.99 per month. Compared to GeForce Now, the game selection is significantly smaller, with the Ultimate tier having over 500 games.

items.title: From the Anime to the Game — Free Update Brings Edgerunners 2 Content and More to Cyberpunk 2077!
items.summary: The free Edgerunners 2 Update to Cyberpunk 2077 is available now, with content inspired by the second installment of the hit anime series now streaming on Netflix
items.content:
“Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2” premiered on Netflix on October 20, bringing a whole new cast of characters to Night City for a dark, gritty ride. And now we’re bringing a little piece of that story into Cyberpunk 2077 , too! The free Edgerunners 2 Update is here, with content inspired by the anime, new ways to fight, more customization options, and plenty of other additions.

We’ve got a lot to cover, so let’s get into it. And don’t worry if you haven’t watched the new anime yet — no “Edgerunners 2” spoilers ahead!

One of the things we love about Night City is that there’s always another story unfolding somewhere. V may be central to the events of Cyberpunk 2077 , but they’re hardly the only merc in town, fighting to survive and make a name for themselves on those neon-soaked streets. Every fixer has clients, every crew has gigs to take care of, every Night City merc has their story — and sometimes, those stories collide in unexpected ways.

That’s exactly what happens in the brand-new quest introduced with the “Edgerunners 2” Update. What begins as just another gig from Wakako turns into an action-packed, high-stakes mission that sees V cross paths with Weak Kingsley, a famed Night City merc and one of the main characters of “Edgerunners 2.” We won’t spoil what happens, but during the course of this mission, V has a chance to assist Weak and his crew during a risky gig that takes place in a brand-new location: Night City Prison.

The new “Edgerunners 2” gig is more than a chance to encounter characters from the anime in the game — it serves as a prequel to the events of the series. So, play the quest before watching the anime, and you’ll have a little extra context going into Episode 1. Already seen the show? Then with this gig, you’ll get to revisit part of Weak’s story with a broader perspective of him and his crew.

And there’s even more forEdgerunnersfans in this update. For starters, you can find and equip Weak’s full outfit — vest, glasses, coat, pants, the works — and get your hands on his signature revolver, Coronation. We’ve also added a new radio station, HKGN 102.FM, featuring official tracks from both “Cyberpunk: Edgerunners” and “Edgerunners 2.” So if you’re planning to spend a few more hours cruising around Night City after watching the show, we’ve got your soundtrack covered.

What’s better than blasting your way through a warehouse full of gangoons with a revolver, dealing one headshot after another? Doing it with two revolvers, obviously.

That’s right — dual wielding is here! With the Edgerunners 2 Update, you can raise hell with a pistol or revolver in each hand. That’s a whole new vibe — and a whole new level of awesome.

But dual wielding isn’t just about looking cool. It brings a new playstyle and a fresh way to approach combat — in fact, it’s one of the most significant gameplay additions to the game’s combat since Update 2.0 introduced throwing knives. So if you’ve been looking for an excuse to shake up your fighting style, this might just be it.

Cyberware enhances your stats and abilities — but what if it could take your style to the next level, too? That’s where glamdocs come in. These new vendors let you customize the appearance of your cyberware, with 40 styles in different colors to choose from. Fancy a new look for your chrome? Pay them a visit at one (or all) of the five locations across Night City and see what catches your eye.

In a city that lives and dies by appearances, V really can’t afford to pass up any opportunity to shake up their look. On top of cyberware customization, we’ve also added 20 new hairstyles and several clothing sets to give your V the best chance of standing out, even in Night City.

We know how creative the Cyberpunk 2077 community can be, and we’re always curious to see what players come up with. That’s why we’re introducing cross-platform mod support through mod.io integration.

The update adds a Mods panel where you can browse and install supported community-created content directly in the game. It’s a new way to experiment with your experience, and we’re looking forward to seeing how it develops as more mods become available and receive support over time!

We’ve covered some of the bigger additions, but there’s still plenty to find in the Edgerunners 2 Update.

items.content:
Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you!

Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watch the Features Overview video to see some of the new features in action:

And if you want to know even more, read through the list of most important changes below:

Edgerunners Content

  • Added a new side quest, Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. To unlock it, complete The Heist and two gigs for Wakako, then wait for a message from her.

    [/*]

  • Added a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King, which can be obtained during the Clampdown side quest.

    [/*]

  • Added a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring a selection of tracks from the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners series.

    [/*]

Show Off

  • A brand-new clothing collection has arrived in Night City! 5 new outfit sets can now be purchased from certain clothing vendors:

    • Maxiwear: available in Heywood, Arroyo, Little China

      [/*]

    • Jinguji: available in City Center

      [/*]

    • NetWatch: available in Kabuki, Japantown

      [/*]

    • IconAmerica: available in Pacifica, Badlands, Northside

      [/*]

    • And one more set that will hit Night City shelves just a little later...

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • The NUS Infiltrator clothing set can be now purchased from clothing vendors in Kabuki and Japantown.

    [/*]

  • 4 new TWINTONE skins for Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech are now available via Twitch Drops.

    [/*]

  • Some of the hairstyles that were previously exclusive to NPCs are now available for V. Please note that some hairstyles are available only to feminine or masculine body types.

    [/*]

  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

    [/*]

  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.

    [/*]

  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.

    [/*]

  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

    [/*]

Mod the World

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.

    [/*]

  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

  • Saves in the “Load Game” menu are now grouped by separate playthroughs.

    [/*]

  • Added item filters to apartment and vehicle stashes.

    [/*]

  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several typos in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

    [/*]

items.content:
To survive in Night City, you need someone to watch your back. On the way to the major leagues, V managed to gather a remarkable crew. You could even say, a crew to remember!

From trusted allies to unforgettable personalities, these are the people who helped shape V’s journey through the City of Dreams. This episode of It’s All About You is dedicated to the legendary crew that stood by V through every high and low.

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk 2077 in the most creative ways possible. Don’t forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY

See you in the next episode!

items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.
